not_committed: 56.2 MB of third-party HTML; deliberately outside the repository.
note: One file, so the file-level manifest is one hash. The per-page hashes below are the useful granularity: they let a partial or corrupted copy be localised to specific URLs rather than only detected.
why: The 2026-07-29 raw HTML is the only artefact from which DELTA-BASELINE.json's derivation can be re-verified, and the only rehearsal source that exercises the TEXT checks — the committed html_v1 corpus runs only the five HTML checks, which is why the old_text=None defect was invisible to a corpus-only rehearsal. It was held in an ephemeral session scratchpad. This manifest lets a later session confirm a copy is intact without the original.

copies.medium: WSL2 ext4 on /dev/sdd, inside the VHDX file hosted on the C: volume
NTFS on the D: volume (Disk 0 partition 5), outside the WSL VHDX
copies.role: second copy — the most independent destination available on this machine
survives: a Windows reset that reimages C:
dies_with: an OEM recovery operation that reformats D:
loss or theft of the machine
copies.caveat: D: is the vendor recovery/tools partition (Drivers/, Recover/, Tools/, SWCONF.DAT). It survives a C: reimage, but a vendor recovery operation could reformat it. Hence the third copy on C:.

copies.medium: NTFS on the C: volume (Disk 0 partition 3), outside the WSL VHDX
copies.role: third copy — hedges against D: being reformatted
survives: an OEM recovery operation that reformats D:
dies_with: loss or theft of the machine

independence: PARTIAL, and the limit is physical. Windows reports exactly one physical disk on this machine: Disk 0, 'RS1D0TSSD510', NVMe, 1024209543168 bytes. C: is partition 3 and D: is partition 5 OF THAT SAME DISK, and the WSL2 ext4 filesystem is a VHDX file on C:. So all three copies share one physical device. What the second and third copies DO close is the largest real-world class for a WSL user: anything that destroys the ext4 filesystem or the VHDX (wsl --unregister, a distro reset, filesystem corruption) leaves both NTFS copies untouched, and a C: reimage leaves the D: copy untouched. Calling this 'redundancy' without that qualification would be false.
residual_risk: Unmitigated: failure of physical Disk 0, and loss, theft or destruction of the machine. Both would take all three copies. Closing them needs an off-machine destination, which is outside this project's local-only boundary (no user-to-server data channel; the only outbound traffic is fetching user-specified URLs) and is therefore the user's decision, not this session's. An OneDrive folder exists at /mnt/c/Users/mkuzi/OneDrive and would close it, at the cost of pushing 56.2 MB of third-party HTML into a personal cloud account. NOT DONE — flagged for the user.
verify_with: python3 analysis/verify_capture.py   # exit 0 all copies verified, 2 a copy is missing, 3 a copy is present but corrupt, 4 this manifest is unusable. Run it before anything relies on the archive.
